I have everything needed. Here is my report.

## Summary

This is a **Go** project (usememos/memos). **Redis is NOT used anywhere.** The cache layer is a custom, hand-rolled **thread-safe in-memory cache with TTL**, built on Go's `sync.Map`.

## 1. Redis usage: NONE

A repository-wide search for `redis`, `Redis`, `ioredis`, `REDIS_URL`, and connection strings across all Go, config, `go.mod`, `go.sum`, YAML, and Markdown files returned **zero matches**. There is no Redis client, no Redis import, no Redis config, and no memcached. The only cache-related third-party library present is `hashicorp/golang-lru/v2 v2.0.7` (in `/bench/repo/go.sum` lines 136-137), but it is a transitive/indirect dependency only — it is **not** in `go.mod` as a direct require and is **not imported by any Go source file** (grep for `hashicorp/golang-lru` and `lru.` in `*.go` returns nothing). So even LRU is not actually used for caching.

## 2. Actual caching mechanism: custom in-memory TTL cache

Implementation: `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go`

- Backed by `sync.Map` with an `atomic.Int64` item counter (lines 66-73).
- Each entry is an `item{ value any; expiration time.Time; size int }` (lines 34-39).
- `Config` struct (lines 41-54): `DefaultTTL`, `CleanupInterval`, `MaxItems`, `OnEviction` callback.
- `DefaultConfig()` (lines 56-64): DefaultTTL = 10 min, CleanupInterval = 5 min, MaxItems = 1000.
- TTL is applied on write: `SetWithTTL` sets `expiration: time.Now().Add(ttl)` (line 112); `Set` uses `c.config.DefaultTTL` (line 94).
- Lazy expiration on read: `Get` deletes and misses if `time.Now().After(itm.expiration)` (lines 135-144).
- Background cleanup goroutine `cleanupLoop` runs on `CleanupInterval` ticker (lines 199-215), calling `cleanup()` which purges expired items (lines 217-250).
- Capacity eviction: when count exceeds `MaxItems`, `cleanupOldest()` removes ~20% oldest-by-expiration items (lines 252-313). This is an approximate/oldest-expiration eviction, **not** a true LRU.
- `estimateSize` is a rough byte estimator (lines 315-327) but size is not actually enforced as a limit anywhere.

Interface defined at `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go` lines 10-32 (`Set`, `SetWithTTL`, `Get`, `Delete`, `Clear`, `Size`, `Close`).

## 3. Cache wiring and configuration in the Store

`/bench/repo/store/store.go`:
- The `Store` holds three cache instances (lines 26-29): `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache`.
- All three are constructed in `New` with a shared `cacheConfig` (lines 40-53):
  - `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`
  - `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`
  - `MaxItems: 1000`
  - `OnEviction: nil`
- `Close()` stops all three cache goroutines (lines 72-79).

## 3 (specific). User cache and TTL applied to user entries

`/bench/repo/store/user.go`:
- Cache key builder: `userCacheKey(userID int32)` returns `strconv.Itoa(int(userID))` (lines 88-90).
- Users are written into `userCache` via plain `Set` (which uses the DefaultTTL of **10 minutes**) at:
  - `CreateUser` — line 98
  - `CreateUserIfNoUsers` — line 122
  - `UpdateUser` — line 132
  - `ListUsers` — line 143 (caches every listed user)
  - `GetUser` — line 167
- `GetUser` reads from cache only when looking up by `ID` (lines 149-156); it type-asserts to `*User`. Lookups by any other field (e.g. username) bypass the cache and hit `ListUsers`.
- Cache invalidation on delete: `DeleteUser` calls `s.deleteUserCache(...)` (line 179), defined in `/bench/repo/store/user_delete.go` line 39.

Note on user-entry TTL: there is **no custom/per-user TTL** — user entries always use the store-wide `DefaultTTL` of 10 minutes. `SetWithTTL` exists on the cache but is not called for user entries (no call sites in the store for users; all user writes use `Set`).

Related caches (same 10-min TTL config):
- User settings: `/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go`, with key helper `getUserSettingCacheKey` in `/bench/repo/store/cache.go` lines 7-9 (`fmt.Sprintf("%d-%s", userID, key)`).
- Instance settings: `/bench/repo/store/instance_setting.go`.

Tests covering cache behavior: `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache_test.go` and `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/instance_admin_cache_test.go` (verifies admin retrieval is served from the Store-layer cache).

### Bottom line
Redis is not used at all. Caching is an in-house, in-memory, TTL-based cache (`sync.Map` + background cleanup + oldest-expiration eviction) configured uniformly at 10-minute TTL / 5-minute cleanup / 1000 max items. User entries are cached by numeric ID with the default 10-minute TTL; no user-specific TTL is applied.
